title.narrative: Promoting awareness and advocacy of the human security approach in overcoming the covid-19 pandemic in vulnerable communities in Cabo Verde

description.narrative:
Cabo Verde presents high rates of urbanization (70%), and some cities, such as Espargos and Sal-Rei, face dramatic figures of more than 300% of urban population growth in the last 15 years. This growth has not been matched by adequate urban services, in particular concerning public spaces, which have been grown even more in relevance due to the pandemic.
The country is strategically located in between America, Africa, and Europe. Combined with its natural beauty and diversity, the country has increasingly become a tourist destination, sparking some of the population growth as mentioned above, of combined domestic and international migration. Nevertheless, the location also places the country as a target for the movement of drugs and other illicit products which, combined with poor urban planning practices, has resulted in the increase of several social issues, including urban crime.
Cabo Verde’s dependency on tourism means it has been one of the hardest hit by the pandemic. For reference, around 20 thousand jobs were lost, for a total population of fewer than 600 thousand people. Therefore, there is an urgent need for initiatives that holistically tackle issues of safety and poor urban planning practices, engaging especially with the youth, most involved in crime, and women, the ones who have suffered the most from the pandemic impact. This project has as main objective to overcome the threats posed by the COVID-19 pandemic to the most vulnerable communities in urban settings of the cities of Espargos, Sal Rei, and Praia in Cabo Verde by promoting awareness and advocacy on the relevance of the human security approach as a key response component via collaborative placemaking and peaceful coexistence.
It is built upon two main elements: • Application of human security approaches at the community level, via collaborative placemaking using the Block by Block approach to support the development of community-based human security action plans (Outcome 1). • Institutionalization of the experience of applying the human security approach at the community level via its incorporation into Local Development Plans for the three cities (Outcome 2). The program will have a duration of 18 months, and will be implemented jointly by UNODC and UN-Habitat in partnership with the Ministries of Justice and Labour (MJT), Infrastructure, Spatial Planning and Housing (MIOTH), Health and Social Security (MSSS), the Municipalities of Praia, Sal and Boa Vista and local NGOs. The three communities in which the project focus are key partners of the project; they are already engaged with UN-Habitat, UNODC, and their national partners working through awareness and empowerment programs for their people and associations.
